intro: This branch introduces fractions: numbers that describe equal parts of a whole, like one half or three quarters. It focuses on what fractions mean, how to picture them and how to compare them, before any calculating.

II.5.01.what: Understanding that fractions start with cutting a whole into equal parts, and naming those parts.

levels.a: Names equal parts as halves, thirds or fourths.
levels.b: Names equal parts as sixths or eighths.
levels.c: Tells whether a shape is cut into equal parts or not.
levels.d: Names what fraction of a whole a shaded part is.

II.5.02.what: Understanding unit fractions: one single part of a whole, like one half, one third or one tenth.

levels.a: Recognizes one half, one third and one fourth in a picture.
levels.b: Recognizes unit fractions with more parts, like one sixth.
levels.c: Sees that cutting a whole into more parts makes each part smaller.
levels.d: Compares unit fractions, knowing one third is bigger than one eleventh.

II.5.03.what: Using a fraction to describe several equal parts of one whole, like three quarters of a shape.

levels.a: Names the fraction of a shape that is shaded.
levels.b: Knows the bottom number (denominator) counts the equal parts and the top (numerator) counts the ones chosen.
levels.c: Writes a fraction from words, like two thirds.
levels.d: Picks the picture that shows a given fraction.

II.5.04.what: Finding a fraction of a group of things, like two thirds of 18 cookies.

levels.a: Finds one part of a group, such as one half of 10.
levels.b: Finds several parts of a group, such as two thirds of 18.
levels.c: Says what fraction of a group of dots is a certain color.
levels.d: Solves word problems about a fraction of a group.
levels.e: Works backwards: knows a fraction of the total, finds the whole amount.
levels.f: Works back through two giveaways, each a fraction of what's left, to find the start.

II.5.05.what: Placing fractions on a number line, seeing each fraction as a point with its own place among the numbers.

levels.a: Names the size of each equal step between 0 and 1.
levels.b: Names a unit fraction marked on the line.
levels.c: Finds where other fractions sit, like three quarters.
levels.d: Places fractions greater than 1 on a longer number line.

II.5.06.what: Seeing that whole numbers can be written as fractions, like two halves making one.

levels.a: Knows how many equal parts make one whole, as in three thirds make 1.
levels.b: Writes a whole number as a fraction over 1, as in 3 is three over one.
levels.c: Writes a whole number as a fraction with any bottom number, as in 5 is ten halves.
levels.d: Spots which fractions on a number line land on whole numbers.

II.5.07.what: Using pictures to see that different fractions can be the same amount, like one half and five tenths.

levels.a: Uses fraction strips of the same length to find equal fractions.
levels.b: Uses two number lines to find fractions at the same spot.
levels.c: Cuts a shaded square into smaller parts and counts to find an equal fraction.
levels.d: Picks out which fractions are equal to one half and which are not.

II.5.08.what: Finding equal fractions with a rule: multiplying or dividing the top and bottom by the same number.

levels.a: Multiplies top and bottom by the same number to make an equal fraction.
levels.b: Divides top and bottom by the same number to make an equal fraction.
levels.c: Writes a fraction in simplest form, with the smallest possible numbers.
levels.d: Tests whether two fractions are equal.
levels.e: Finds an equal fraction from a second clue, such as how much bigger the bottom is than the top.
levels.f: Finds what number to add to the top and bottom of a fraction to make it equal another.

II.5.09.what: Comparing fractions with the same bottom number, where the parts are the same size.

levels.a: Sees that more parts of the same size is more.
levels.b: Uses the greater than, less than and equals signs to compare.
levels.c: Compares by seeing which fraction is further along a number line.
levels.d: Answers story problems, like who used more ribbon.

II.5.10.what: Comparing fractions with the same top number, where the counts match but the part sizes differ.

levels.a: Sees that one big part beats one small part.
levels.b: Uses the comparison signs, such as two tenths is less than two eighths.
levels.c: Explains why one fifth is more than one seventh.
levels.d: Answers story problems, like who ate more pizza.

II.5.11.what: Comparing any two fractions, even when their tops and bottoms are both different.

levels.a: Decides whether a fraction is less than, equal to or more than one half.
levels.b: Rewrites both fractions with the same bottom number, then compares.
levels.c: Uses a quick cross-multiplying check to compare.
levels.d: Puts a list of fractions in order from least to greatest.
levels.e: Finds the smallest whole number top that makes a fraction bigger than another.
levels.f: Counts how many fractions with a given bottom number fit between two fractions.

II.5.12.what: Understanding mixed numbers: a whole number plus a fraction, like one and three quarters.

levels.a: Reads a mixed number aloud correctly.
levels.b: Names a mixed number marked on a number line.
levels.c: Picks the picture that shows a given mixed number.
levels.d: Puts a whole number and a fraction together as a mixed number.

II.5.13.what: Understanding improper fractions, where the top is bigger than the bottom, like 13 thirds, and switching them to mixed numbers.

levels.a: Recognizes which fractions are greater than 1.
levels.b: Turns an improper fraction into a mixed number.
levels.c: Turns a mixed number into an improper fraction.
levels.d: Compares an improper fraction with a mixed number.
levels.e: Finds a missing bottom or top number so an improper fraction matches a mixed number.
levels.f: Counts every fraction in simplest form, greater than 1, whose top and bottom add to a set total.

II.5.14.what: Seeing a fraction as a division: three quarters is the same as 3 divided by 4.

levels.a: Writes a fraction as a division, and a division as a fraction.
levels.b: Works out each person's share when pizzas are shared equally.
levels.c: Gives a division answer as a mixed number, as in 9 divided by 2 is four and a half.
levels.d: Solves sharing word problems with mixed-number answers.

II.5.15.what: Building a feel for how big a fraction is without exact calculation.

levels.a: Understands that two thirds of a big cake is more than two thirds of a small one.
levels.b: Tells whether a fraction is close to 0, one half or 1.
levels.c: Estimates a sum of fractions by rounding each to a nearby easy value.
levels.d: Says which of two fractions is greater and explains why.
